audit_status.source_base: Greek 2 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Macedonia generosity, grace of giving, Messiah's poverty/riches, equality, Titus, honorable administration.

verses.restored: Now we make known to you, siblings, the grace of the Divine given in the assemblies of Macedonia,

familiar.text: Moreover, brethren, we do you to wit of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia;

modern.text: Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia.

original.text: Γνωρίζομεν δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δεδομένην ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Μακεδονίας,

verses.restored: that in much testing of pressure, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded into the riches of their generosity.

familiar.text: How that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.

modern.text: In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.

original.text: ὅτι ἐν πολλῇ δοκιμῇ θλίψεως ἡ περισσεία τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία αὐτῶν ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς ⸂τὸ πλοῦτος⸃ τῆς ἁπλότητος αὐτῶν·

verses.restored: For according to power, I testify, and beyond power, of their own accord,

familiar.text: For to their power, I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves;

modern.text: For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,

original.text: ὅτι κατὰ δύναμιν, μαρτυρῶ, καὶ ⸀παρὰ δύναμιν, αὐθαίρετοι

verses.restored: with much appeal they begged us for the grace and fellowship/participation of the service to the holy ones,

familiar.text: Praying us with much intreaty that we would receive the gift, and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints.

modern.text: they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.

original.text: μετὰ πολλῆς παρακλήσεως δεόμενοι ἡμῶν, τὴν χάριν καὶ τὴν κοινωνίαν τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους—

verses.restored: and not just as we hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and to us through the will of the Divine.

familiar.text: And this they did, not as we hoped, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God.

modern.text: And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, because it was the will of God.

original.text: καὶ οὐ καθὼς ἠλπίσαμεν ἀλλʼ ἑαυτοὺς ἔδωκαν πρῶτον τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ,

verses.restored: So that we appealed to Titus, that just as he began before, so he might also complete among you this grace also.

familiar.text: Insomuch that we desired Titus, that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also.

modern.text: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.

original.text: εἰς τὸ παρακαλέσαι ἡμᾶς Τίτον ἵνα καθὼς προενήρξατο οὕτως καὶ ἐπιτελέσῃ εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ τὴν χάριν ταύτην·

verses.restored: But just as you abound in everything, in trust and word and knowledge and all eagerness and the love from us in you, so also abound in this grace.

familiar.text: Therefore, as ye abound in every thing, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all diligence, and in your love to us, see that ye abound in this grace also.

modern.text: But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you —see that you also excel in this grace of giving.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ὥσπερ ἐν παντὶ περισσεύετε, πίστει καὶ λόγῳ καὶ γνώσει καὶ πάσῃ σπουδῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξ ⸂ἡμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν⸃ ἀγάπῃ, ἵνα καὶ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ χάριτι περισσεύητε.

verses.restored: I do not speak according to command, but through the eagerness of others testing the genuineness of your love.

familiar.text: I speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the forwardness of others, and to prove the sincerity of your love.

modern.text: I am not making a demand, but I am testing the sincerity of your love in comparison to the earnestness of others.

original.text: Οὐ κατʼ ἐπιταγὴν λέγω ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς ἑτέρων σπουδῆς καὶ τὸ τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀγάπης γνήσιον δοκιμάζων·

verses.restored: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Messiah, that though being rich, because of you he became poor, so that you by his poverty might become rich.

familiar.text: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.

modern.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.

original.text: γινώσκετε γὰρ τὴν χάριν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅτι διʼ ὑμᾶς ἐπτώχευσεν πλούσιος ὤν, ἵνα ὑμεῖς τῇ ἐκείνου πτωχείᾳ πλουτήσητε.

verses.restored: And in this I give judgment; for this benefits you, who began before, not only to do but also to will, since last year.

familiar.text: And herein I give my advice: for this is expedient for you, who have begun before, not only to do, but also to be forward a year ago.

modern.text: And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.

original.text: καὶ γνώμην ἐν τούτῳ δίδωμι· τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν συμφέρει, οἵτινες οὐ μόνον τὸ ποιῆσαι ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ θέλειν προενήρξασθε ἀπὸ πέρυσι·

verses.restored: But now complete the doing also, so that just as the eagerness to will was present, so also the completing from what you have.

familiar.text: Now therefore perform the doing of it; that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which ye have.

modern.text: Now finish the work, so that you may complete it just as eagerly as you began, according to your means.

original.text: νυνὶ δὲ καὶ τὸ ποιῆσαι ἐπιτελέσατε, ὅπως καθάπερ ἡ προθυμία τοῦ θέλειν οὕτως καὶ τὸ ἐπιτελέσαι ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν.

verses.restored: For if the eagerness is present, it is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.

familiar.text: For if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not.

modern.text: For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ἡ προθυμία πρόκειται, καθὸ ἐὰν ⸀ἔχῃ εὐπρόσδεκτος, οὐ καθὸ οὐκ ἔχει.

verses.restored: For not that there be relief to others and pressure to you, but from equality:

familiar.text: For I mean not that other men be eased, and ye burdened:

modern.text: It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.

original.text: οὐ γὰρ ἵνα ἄλλοις ἄνεσις, ⸀ὑμῖν θλῖψις· ἀλλʼ ἐξ ἰσότητος

verses.restored: at the present season your abundance for their lack, so that their abundance also may come to be for your lack, so that there may be equality,

familiar.text: But by an equality, that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their want, that their abundance also may be a supply for your want: that there may be equality:

modern.text: At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. Then there will be equality.

original.text: ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ τὸ ὑμῶν περίσσευμα εἰς τὸ ἐκείνων ὑστέρημα, ἵνα καὶ τὸ ἐκείνων περίσσευμα γένηται εἰς τὸ ὑμῶν ὑστέρημα, ὅπως γένηται ἰσότης·

verses.restored: just as it is written: The one with much did not have excess, and the one with little did not lack.

familiar.text: As it is written, He that had gathered much had nothing over; and he that had gathered little had no lack.

modern.text: As it is written: “He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.” Titus Commended (Titus 1:1–4)

original.text: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ τὸ πολὺ οὐκ ἐπλεόνασεν, καὶ ὁ τὸ ὀλίγον οὐκ ἠλαττόνησεν.

verses.restored: But thanks to the Divine, who gives the same eagerness for you in the heart of Titus,

familiar.text: But thanks be to God, which put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you.

modern.text: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.

original.text: Χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ τῷ ⸀διδόντι τὴν αὐτὴν σπουδὴν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ Τίτου,

verses.restored: because he indeed received the appeal, but being more eager, of his own accord he went out to you.

familiar.text: For indeed he accepted the exhortation; but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you.

modern.text: For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.

original.text: ὅτι τὴν μὲν παράκλησιν ἐδέξατο, σπουδαιότερος δὲ ὑπάρχων αὐθαίρετος ἐξῆλθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: And we sent with him the sibling whose praise in the good news is through all the assemblies,

familiar.text: And we have sent with him the brother, whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches;

modern.text: Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.

original.text: συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ μετʼ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀδελφὸν οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διὰ πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν—

verses.restored: and not only this, but also having been appointed by the assemblies as our traveling companion with this grace being served by us, toward the glory of the Lord and our eagerness,

familiar.text: And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind:

modern.text: More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the offering —the gracious gift we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.

original.text: οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ χειροτονηθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν συνέκδημος ἡμῶν ⸀σὺν τῇ χάριτι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφʼ ἡμῶν πρὸς τὴν ⸀αὐτοῦ τοῦ κυρίου δόξαν καὶ προθυμίαν ἡμῶν—

verses.restored: avoiding this: that anyone should blame us in this abundance being served by us.

familiar.text: Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us:

modern.text: We hope to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.

original.text: στελλόμενοι τοῦτο μή τις ἡμᾶς μωμήσηται ἐν τῇ ἁδρότητι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφʼ ἡμῶν,

verses.restored: For we take thought beforehand for beautiful/good things, not only before the Lord but also before humans.

familiar.text: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

modern.text: For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.

original.text: ⸂προνοοῦμεν γὰρ⸃ καλὰ οὐ μόνον ἐνώπιον κυρίου ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐνώπιον ἀνθρώπων.

verses.restored: And we sent with them our sibling whom we have often tested and found eager in many things, but now much more eager by great confidence toward you.

familiar.text: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have oftentimes proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent, upon the great confidence which I have in you.

modern.text: And we are sending along with them our brother whose earnestness has been proven many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.

original.text: συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ αὐτοῖς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν ὃν ἐδοκιμάσαμεν ἐν πολλοῖς πολλάκις σπουδαῖον ὄντα, νυνὶ δὲ πολὺ σπουδαιότερον πεποιθήσει πολλῇ τῇ εἰς ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: Whether concerning Titus, he is my partner and coworker for you; whether our siblings, they are apostles/messengers of assemblies, glory of Messiah.

familiar.text: Whether any do enquire of Titus, he is my partner and fellowhelper concerning you: or our brethren be enquired of, they are the messengers of the churches, and the glory of Christ.

modern.text: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, to the glory of Christ.

original.text: εἴτε ὑπὲρ Τίτου, κοινωνὸς ἐμὸς καὶ εἰς ὑμᾶς συνεργός· εἴτε ἀδελφοὶ ἡμῶν, ἀπόστολοι ἐκκλησιῶν, δόξα Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore show to them, before the face of the assemblies, the proof of your love and of our boasting on your behalf.

familiar.text: Wherefore shew ye to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.

modern.text: In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.

original.text: τὴν οὖν ἔνδειξιν τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν καυχήσεως ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν εἰς αὐτοὺς ⸀ἐνδεικνύμενοι εἰς πρόσωπον τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν.

translation_notes: Giving is called grace repeatedly; generosity is participation, not coercion.
Paul's collection logic is equality: abundance meeting lack so no one has excess and no one lacks.
